clue.text: Sensible allowance nearly everyone will make

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

indicators.note: nearly means the word for everyone stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A fair share handed out to almost all is the sensible arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A rational choice is a reasonable, level-headed one, a synonym of sensible.

clue.text: He'll lecture about a German article

parts.note: re means about, concerning
der is German for the

explanation.surface: Someone will give a talk about a German grammar point.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader is a senior lecturer, just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities this rank of academic gives lectures, ranking just below a professor.

clue.text: Sort of cigarettes that must be listed

definitions.meaning: cigarettes with a filter on the end
leaning over, as a ship that lists does

explanation.definitionFit: Filter cigarettes have a filter on the end, and a ship that lists has leaned over.

clue.text: None fly when due

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means none
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Nobody takes to the air when the time comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Money due is money still outstanding to be paid, a synonym.

clue.text: This is simple, so there aren't any pictures

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as without art, lacking pictures

explanation.definitionFit: Naive and guileless means simple, and taken apart the word reads as lacking art.

clue.text: Fondle and be solicitous with some craft

parts.note: to care is to be solicitous, concerned for someone
SS stands for steamship, a craft on the water

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stroke tenderly and show concern, with a little skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To fondle is to stroke lovingly, which is what a tender touch of this kind does.

clue.text: Directs a dunderhead over clothing

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the earlier pieces above the clothing

parts.note: the head of the word dunder is its first letter, D
dresses are clothing

explanation.surface: An idiot is put in charge of a costume department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like an insult, but split it reads as the head (first letter) of 'dunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct a letter is to write its destination on it, a synonym.

clue.text: The service balanced strain

parts.note: even means balanced, level
a strain is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A church service is a well-balanced piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, an example of a church service.

clue.text: Let's get up late, just like the stars!

indicators.note: get up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A suggestion to rise late like the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate means star-shaped, radiating from a centre as a star does.

clue.text: Delegates a page and tips

parts.note: points are tips, as the sharp ends of things

explanation.surface: Someone names representatives and hands a messenger boy some advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate someone is to name or assign them to a role, a synonym of nominate.

clue.text: Hold on-not all are glad hereabouts

indicators.note: not all of these words are used, so a run of letters is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone clings on, though not everyone around here is happy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast or cling, a synonym of the phrasal verb hold on.

clue.text: A boss some think nobody could please

indicators.note: some means only part of these words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A manager whom certain people believe nobody could satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a rounded stud or protruding lump, as a handle is.

clue.text: Daphne is constantly mindful of the environment

parts.note: ever means always, constantly
green means environmentally conscious

explanation.surface: A woman named Daphne is always an eco-warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne looks like a woman's name, but it is a genus of shrubs, most of which keep their leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a genus of shrubs, an example of a plant that keeps its foliage through winter.

clue.text: Calm sovereign, a supporter of art

parts.note: ease means calm, freedom from strain
a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L (from libra) is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A serene monarch is a great patron of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound, so it stands for L, the pound symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand holds the canvas upright, literally supporting a work of art.

clue.text: Food for poachers?

parts.note: poachers suggests illegal hunters, but here it means pans used to poach breakfast food in simmering water

explanation.definitionFit: A poacher is a pan for cooking these in water, so they are the food it is meant for.

clue.text: Fruit warmed up is offensive stuff

parts.note: grapes are fruit
heated means hot

explanation.surface: Heated-up fruit is unpleasant to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot was clusters of small iron balls fired from cannon, ammunition for attack.

clue.text: Sort of helmet that's best in a melee

indicators.note: a melee is a confused scrum, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A type of headgear is the finest thing to wear in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinet is a light medieval steel helmet, an example of protective headgear.

clue.text: Distressed as a herd's broken up

indicators.note: broken up signals that the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Upset because a group of cattle has scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassed means worn down and troubled by pressure, a synonym of distressed.

clue.text: The beast a guy bore

parts.note: a guy is a man
to drill is to bore a hole

explanation.surface: The monster is a tedious fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandrill is a large West African baboon, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: It's so hard for a worker after a stoppage

indicators.note: after places the insect worker behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: a dam stops the flow of water
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Things are tough for a labourer once a blockage stops the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant was a legendary stone of supreme hardness, so the word itself names something exceedingly hard.

clue.text: Retrieved a Roman robe

parts.note: retrieved means got back, and got written back gives these three letters

explanation.surface: Someone recovered a garment from ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrieved' is read as 'got back': GOT reversed gives TOG, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Put off certain players

definitions.meaning: to throw off or shed, as a snake does its skin
the actors chosen for a particular play or film

explanation.definitionFit: Shedding a skin is to throw it off, and a company of actors in one production is its line-up.

clue.text: Given little money, admitting maybe not being satisfied

indicators.note: admitting means the coin takes in other letters

parts.note: a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters of not are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone handed a pittance admits perhaps not being happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a link word here; 'maybe' is the anagram signal working only on the short word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be content is to be pleased with what one has, a synonym.

clue.text: A country road circumventing a regulation

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the road surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI
a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: A rural lane goes round a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: Jack has aged so badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jack has got old terribly fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack is slang for a sailor, as is an old salt.

clue.text: A minister the French find confused

definitions.note: the answer is usually a verb meaning to muddle, but as an adjective it means muddled, as in an addle egg

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a title held by a clergyman
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people find a clergyman bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Addle as an adjective means muddled or rotten, as in an addle-headed person.

clue.text: Trap one without a friend in a drinking-place

indicators.note: without means outside, so the trap and the one surround the friend

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching game
an ace is a one in cards
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Snare a lonely person with no mates at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside: GIN and ACE stand either side of PAL. A gin palace was a showy Victorian pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace was a gaudy nineteenth-century tavern, an example of a public house.

clue.text: Ophidian computer

definitions.meaning: one who computes or adds up figures

explanation.definitionFit: A viper is a snake, and someone who totals figures computes them.

clue.text: Little light's required

definitions.meaning: small or slender in size or degree
light in weight or build, as a slender figure is

explanation.definitionFit: A slender figure is both small and lightweight, so the word covers both senses.

clue.text: Fillet with pate set before a group of music men

indicators.note: set before places the word for the pate ahead of the group

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Fish fillet with liver pâté is served before the musicians play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fillet' looks culinary, beside a 'pate' that suggests pâté, but a fillet is also a ribbon worn round the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet is a narrow ribbon tied round the hair, the same as a strip worn on the brow.

clue.text: 549 at one point — swell!

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and IL is 49
taken as written
E is east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at hitting a score of 549.
explanation.walkthrough: IL for 49 is a loose crossword form of Roman numerals (strictly XLIX).
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or expand, a synonym of the verb swell.

clue.text: 23 is seen to be in pain, and that's disturbing

indicators.note: to be in places the sailor inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
23 down is a jack or old sailor, and a tar is another word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is seen suffering, and that is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' points to the answer at 23 down; a synonym of that answer is used, not its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To start game is to rouse or flush it from cover, so this means rousing or unsettling.
